newsitem.title: UK: Britain to ban transplant of pig hearts, paper.
newsitem.headline: Britain to ban transplant of pig hearts, paper.

text.p: The British government will on Thursday announce a ban on pioneering surgery to transplant pig hearts into people, the Times newspaper reported.
It said a government inquiry had concluded that the procedure was too risky.
Doctors had hoped to carry out the first operations late last year but were forbidden to do so amid fears that the animal organs might carry viruses that could prove deadly to human beings.

Health Secretary Stephen Dorrell has decided that no trials involving people should take place yet and that new laws are needed to establish a regulatory body to control experiments, the Times said. No official comment was immediately available.
The Times said the decision would come as a blow to thousands of people awaiting transplants.
It said 25 patients, including cystic fibrosis sufferers, had already been identified as the first potential recipients of pig hearts. At least 6,000 people are awaiting heart transplants in Britain.
